# Round 2 / Branch 4b: How AI agents can build Minecraft maps at high quality and large scale (2026-10-13)

Scope: write paths for code-made builds on **Java 1.21.1 (DataVersion 3955) + NeoForge**, generation methods, LLM-building research 2023-2026, GPU-free review loops, and a recommended building pipeline for our map (Sewer Town-SW, Outer-Wall Ruins-Slums first).
Not repeated here: general agent orchestration (docs/pipeline/README.md), build tools overview (docs/research/sources/notes_gameplay.md "Building tools": Axiom Fabric-only/ARR, WorldEdit 7.3.8, WorldPainter 2.27, Amulet 0.10.57).

Tags: **[V]** verified in an official doc, primary source or by my own test today · **[V-local]** I ran it in this cloud container today · **[C]** community/second-hand · **[?]** unverified or my inference.
Raw search/fetch JSON: `research/r2/4b/` (S_*.json, F_*.json). Test scripts: `research/r2/4b_scripts/`. Test renders: `research/r2/4b/test_module.png`, `research/r2/4b/big.png`.

---

## 0. Ten-line summary

1. **Primary write path = vanilla structure `.nbt` files with `DataVersion 3955`**, generated by code, stored in our datapack under `data/<ns>/structure/` (singular folder since 1.21), placed with `/place template` (1.19+) or loaded by GameTests. Keep a text twin (SNBT) or the generator code in git for diffs. [V]
2. 1.21.1 has **no `/place ... strict`** (added 1.21.5) → `/place template` triggers block updates; for update-free pastes use WorldEdit 7.3.8 `//perf neighbors off` / `//perf update off`. [V]
3. **GDMC-HTTP (live HTTP editing) has no 1.21.1 build** (1.20.2, 1.21.4, 1.21.11 only; one jar for Fabric+NeoForge, MIT). For 1.21.1: port it (MIT) or use offline generation + RCON `/place`. [V]
4. **LLM-only building is still weak on reliability**: MineCEraft (Aug 2026) best <40% strict task success vs humans ~90%; MineAnyBuild GPT-4o 41/100 on raw block matrices. **Code-as-action with primitives** is what scales (MineBench: models write JS against `block/box/line`; Opus 5.5 is #3 at Elo 2188, GPT-6 Astra Pro #1 2280, GPT-6.1 Sol Pro #2 2213). [V]
5. **GDMC lesson:** ML/generative entries "scored rather poorly with judges"; the 2025 winner **hand-made a set of buildings** and spent his effort on layout/terrain/pathing (Gaussian-filtered heightmaps, water-particle path merging). Runner-ups: districts → roads on seams → buildings in blocks → decorated "nooks"; data-driven palettes with weathering; NBT modules with rotation. [V]
6. What worked in LLM 3D research: **plan as a graph/blueprint → code → deterministic constraint checks → render → critique → fix**, plus a **growing skill/module library** and **API-doc retrieval** (SceneCraft +45% CLIP, constraint pass 88.9 vs 5.6; LL3M planner/coder/critic/verifier/user loop; APT memory module A/B gain). [V]
7. **Headless CPU rendering works in this cloud container today**: deepslate 0.27.2 + headless-gl under Xvfb rendered a 1.21.1 structure with vanilla 1.21.1 textures in ~6 s (64×24×64, 8k blocks, 1024×768). [V-local]
8. For the user: the **ewanhowell structure-viewer** web app opens `.nbt/.schem/.litematic`, layers resource packs and **mod jars**, can pin a game version (1.21.1), walks in first person, assembles jigsaw pools, and has a **compare mode that highlights new/changed/removed blocks** — a ready-made diff/review tool. [V]
9. Chunky (path tracer) is a poor fit: stable 2.4.6 stops at 1.20.4, 2.5.0 snapshot needed for 1.21, **no mod blocks/custom models**, needs a world save not a structure. Use it only for vanilla-block beauty shots. [V]
10. Recommended pipeline: **contracts (palette + layout graph + module grid) → agent-made module kit (user-approved) → seeded Python assembler → deterministic validators (block states, walkability/reachability BFS, support, light/BE budgets, diff) → headless render sheet + structure-viewer link → user approval → RCON/WorldEdit placement on a 1.21.1 NeoForge server → GameTests + in-game shader screenshots on the user's PC.**

## 1. Write paths for 1.21.1

### 1.1 Vanilla structure files (`.nbt`) — recommended primary format
- **Format** [V] https://minecraft.wiki/w/Structure_file : gzipped NBT root with `DataVersion` (int), `size` [x,y,z], `palette` (list of `{Name, Properties}`) **or** `palettes` (list of palettes; "a random palette gets selected based on coordinates. Used in vanilla by shipwrecks" → usable for clean/ruined material variants of the same geometry), `blocks` (list of `{state, pos, nbt?}`; block-entity `nbt` without x/y/z), `entities` (list of `{pos (double), blockPos (int), nbt}`).
- **Location** [V]: `data/<namespace>/structure/*.nbt` (renamed from `structures` in 1.21 / 24w21a). Structure blocks save to `<world>/generated/<ns>/structure/`.
- **1.21.1 data version = 3955**, resource pack format 34 [V] https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_1.21.1
- **Item NBT inside containers must use the 1.20.5+ component format** (`count`, `components`), because the file claims DataVersion 3955 and will not be data-fixed. LLMs often emit the old `Count`/`tag` format. [V] https://minecraft.wiki/w/Item_format/Before_1.20.5 ; [?] on how often LLMs get it wrong — make it a validator rule.
- **Text twin for git**: the vanilla data generator converts `.nbt` ↔ `.snbt` (`java -DbundlerMainClass=net.minecraft.data.Main -jar server.jar --dev --input in --output out`) and dumps `--reports` (blocks.json with every block state, registries, command tree). [V] https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial:Running_the_data_generator . In 1.21.1 `StructureTemplateManager` also has `loadFromSnbt`/`loadFromTestStructures` (SNBT test structures) [V] https://lexxie.dev/neoforge/1.21.1/net/minecraft/world/level/levelgen/structure/templatesystem/StructureTemplateManager.html . nbtlib SNBT round-trip tested equal [V-local].
- **Placing**:
  - `/place template <id> [pos] [rotation none|clockwise_90|counterclockwise_90|180] [mirror none|front_back|left_right] [integrity 0..1] [seed]` (1.19+). `strict` (no block/shape updates) only from **1.21.5** → not in 1.21.1. `/place jigsaw` max depth 20 since 1.20.5. Target chunks must be loaded (use `/forceload`). [V] https://minecraft.wiki/w/Commands/place
  - Structure Block UI limit is **48×48×48** in Java (offset ≤48) [V] https://minecraft.wiki/w/Structure_Block . Files written by code are not bound by this UI limit [C/?]; still tile big areas (see §5) for memory, diffs and chunk loading.
  - `integrity` + `seed` gives cheap deterministic decay at placement time [V].
- **GameTest** loads `.nbt` templates from `data/<ns>/structure` → encounter rooms double as test scenes [V] https://docs.neoforged.net/docs/1.21.1/misc/gametest

### 1.2 Jigsaw / datapack worldgen
- Jigsaw structure config: `size` 0–20 depth; `max_distance_from_center` 1–128 (≤116 with terrain adaptation); `dimension_padding`, `liquid_settings` added in 1.21; per-axis `max_distance_from_center` only from 1.21.9 (not ours). Template pools with weights, fallbacks, processors. [V] https://minecraft.wiki/w/Jigsaw_structure
- For a **hand-authored adventure map**, worldgen jigsaw is optional: assembly at worldgen time is random and harder to review. Better: **assemble offline with our own seeded code** that mimics jigsaw sockets, write the result as tiles, and keep vanilla jigsaw only for repeatable filler (e.g., slum shack clusters) if wanted. [?] The structure-viewer below can preview real jigsaw assemblies seeded and reproducibly. [V]

### 1.3 Sponge `.schem` v3 and WorldEdit
- Spec v3 (2021-05-04): root `Schematic` compound, `Version`=3, `DataVersion`, `Width/Height/Length` (unsigned short), `Offset`, `Blocks` container (palette + varint data + block entities), optional `Biomes` (3D), `Entities`; gzip; extension `.schem`. [V] https://github.com/SpongePowered/Schematic-Specification/blob/master/versions/schematic-3.md
- WorldEdit 7.3 reads/writes v3 by default (`/schem save name sponge.2` for v2) [V] https://madelinemiller.dev/blog/introducing-worldedit-7-3/ ; **WorldEdit 7.3.8 NeoForge/Fabric for 1.21–1.21.1** [V] https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/worldedit/files/5830452
- Paste without updates: `//perf neighbors off` / `//perf update off` (maintainer reply, Jul 2026) [V] https://github.com/EngineHub/WorldEdit/issues/2991
- **CraftScripts** (`/cs file args`, JS via Rhino): Rhino is a separate download renamed `js.jar` into `mods/`; scripts in `config/worldedit/craftscripts/`; globals `context`, `player`, `argv`; `context.remember()` gives one undoable EditSession [V] https://world-edit.com/craftscripts/ , https://github.com/EngineHub/WorldEditDocs/blob/master/source/usage/other/craftscripts.rst . Needs a player to invoke [?]; useful for in-game brushes on the user's PC, not for headless CI.

### 1.4 Litematica `.litematic`
- Version map: v5 (1.13–1.17) < v6 (1.18–1.20.4) < **v7 (1.20.5+)**; SubVersion 1 cosmetic [V] https://docs.rs/nucleation/latest/nucleation/formats/litematic/index.html
- NeoForge 1.21.1 port: **Forgematica 0.4.1+mc1.21.1** (LGPL-3.0, needs MaFgLib) [V] https://modrinth.com/mod/forgematica/version/bNQ9lJbg . Gives in-game ghost overlay + Schematic Verifier for checking a placed build against the file [? verifier on the port].
- litemapy 0.11.0b0 (GPLv3) defaults to `lm_version=6, mc_version=2975` → **must pass `lm_version=7, mc_version=3955`** for 1.21.1 [V-local] https://litemapy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/schematic.html

## 2. Generation methods

### 2.1 What GDMC (AI settlement generation) teaches
- Competition: algorithm builds an "interesting" settlement on an unseen map; human judges score **Adaptation to terrain, Functionality (embodied), Narrative, Aesthetics**. 2025 used MC 1.21.4; 2026 used **1.21.11**, 10 entries, results at CoG 2026 (September; result table not yet on wiki when checked) [V] https://gendesignmc.wikidot.com/wiki:2025-settlement-generation-competition , https://gendesignmc.wikidot.com/wiki:2026-settlement-generation-competition
- **2025 results**: 1st Gaussianly Filtered (5.95; aesthetics 6.54), 2nd Shadow Wizard Money Gang (4.71, best Chronicle), 3rd Panda_Revival (4.62). All 6 entries used the HTTP framework. [V]
- **Winner's method** (Isaac Braam, interview May 2026) [V] https://www.aiandgames.com/p/generative-design-in-minecraft-in :
  - Paths: A* between houses, then each path point is a "water molecule" attracted to neighbours so parallel paths merge and branch naturally.
  - Siting: many Gaussian filters over the heightmap to find good building spots, then another filter to smooth the ground.
  - Buildings: "**I just made a very nice set of buildings**" by hand; "the building part is by far the hardest part and the unsolved part"; buildings "are all if-statements".
  - Post-processing narrative pass: ash gradients over a clean white palette.
  - Organisers: generative/ML entries "have thus far scored rather poorly with judges"; LLMs helped only in the Chronicle (generated books from biome/geometry features).
  - His 2026 idea: LLM plans → image gen → image-to-3D → voxelize; the hard part is the voxel translation (generators "average" and smooth walls; need a translator that straightens walls and snaps doors to Minecraft sizes).
- **Grimoire / TOME** (SWMG, 2nd 2024 and 2025) [V] https://gendesignmc.wikidot.com/wiki:2024-settlement-generation-competition , https://github.com/Jandhi/Tome/ : districts (Voronoi parcels) → merge to superdistricts; off-limits for steep/rough/border districts; urban cluster with a wall; roads along district seams; buildings in blocks; leftover space becomes **"nooks" decorated from configured nook templates**; A* country roads with signage; **data-driven JSON palettes with colour variation and weathering**; NBT structure placement with rotation; OpenAI-generated names/chronicles.
- **2024 winner** Frightful Hobgoblin (Rust, on-disk world format): simulates villagers gathering materials and constructing; changes are replayed as a datapack (~1.5M commands stored in NBT) [V].
- 2024 "Last Minute": Sobel/Gaussian filters on heightmap, skeleton of shape → roads, **modular patterns assembled by conditions** [V]. Niels-NTG 2024: library layout via simple **WFC** [V].
- Judges' hidden criteria (2018–2020 comment analysis): **usability of the environment, thematic coherence, anchoring in real-world simulacra**, plus indexical/environmental storytelling [V] https://uhra.herts.ac.uk/id/eprint/10728/1/Minecraft_Judge_Comments_1_.pdf → maps directly to a soulslike: walkable readable routes, one coherent visual theme per area, believable infrastructure (pipes, drains, shanties), and story told by traces.

### 2.2 Technique menu (and where each fits our map)
| Technique | Evidence | Fit for us |
|---|---|---|
| **Kit-bashing hand-made modules** on a grid with typed sockets | GDMC winners; Grimoire nooks; jigsaw in vanilla | **Core method.** Modules made by agents, approved by the user once per kit, reused many times |
| Graph-first level layout (lock/key, **cyclic generation**: start/goal on a cycle, minor cycles, then convert graph → grid → tiles) | Unexplored (Dormans) [V] https://www.boristhebrave.com/2021/04/10/dungeon-generation-in-unexplored/ | Soulslike shortcuts are cycles back to the checkpoint (AI LIMIT levels loop back to their Branch). Author the layout graph by hand/agent, embed on a coarse grid |
| WFC with socket constraints | Townscaper-style; GDMC 2024 library; MGAIA-Minecraft (Python) [V] https://github.com/ScholliYT/MGAIA-Minecraft | Filler districts (slum roofs, sewer side tunnels) inside hand-placed hero spaces |
| Shape / box-split grammars (CGA) | Box-split grammars in Minecraft (FDG 2022; seen in search results only) [C] https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3555858.3555865 ; SIGI grammar induction from examples [V] https://github.com/gillishermans/sigi | Facades of shacks/towers: split into floors → bays → window/door/balcony slots |
| Noise + filters for terrain/decay | GDMC winners (Gaussian, Sobel) | Weathering masks (moss, cracks, black mud stains), debris scatter, terrain smoothing |
| Data-driven palettes with weathering ramps | Grimoire/TOME | Palette slots per area from the art bible; e.g. `wall_primary: stone_bricks 60 / cracked 25 / mossy 15` |
| Voxelizing 3D models | ObjToSchematic: 1.0 legacy BSD-3 desktop/web, 2.0 web app with AI model generation; exports `.litematic/.schem/.nbt` + **mcfunction datapack**; custom block atlases for modded blocks/resource packs [V] https://github.com/LucasDower/ObjToSchematic , https://objtoschematic.com/wiki ; Hunyuan2Minecraft (GPU) [C] | Only for organic hero shapes (giant roots, statues, flesh masses). Not for architecture (soft walls, wrong door sizes — GDMC winner) |
| Diffusion/transformer voxel models | Dream-Cubed (Sakana/NYU, Jul 2026: inpainting/outpainting at block resolution, trained on billions of cubes) [V] https://sakana.ai/dream-cubed/ ; Block3D (Aug 2026) [V]; BuildingBlock (SIGGRAPH 2025: LLM layout + diffusion + procedural) [V] https://arxiv.org/html/2505.04051v1 | GPU-bound research code; watch, don't depend |
| Heightmap/image → terrain | WorldPainter scripting [V] | Outer-wall ruins terrain base and lake shore; sewer is mostly carved volume |

## 3. LLM-driven building research 2023–2026: what quality, what worked

| Work | Setup | Result | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| **MineBench** (live, Oct 2026) [V] https://minebench.ai/faq , https://github.com/Ammaar-Alam/minebench , https://minebench.ai/api/leaderboard | Model writes **JavaScript against a voxel API (`block`, `box`, `line`)**, sandbox executes, human blind pairwise votes (Bradley-Terry). **One-shot, no render feedback.** | Elo: GPT 6 Astra Pro 2280, GPT 6.1 Sol Pro 2213, **Claude Opus 5.5 2188** (avg 0.58M blocks/build, $7.4, 15 min), GPT 6 Sol Pro 2092, Claude Opus 5 2050, **Sonnet 5.5 2038** ($0.67), Fable 5.1 1966, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1857 ($0.07), GLM 5.3 Flash 1821. Avg builds 0.3–1.5M blocks | Frontier models can now write programs that build very large coherent voxel scenes. GPT-6.1 Sol is close to Opus at ~1/10 cost → useful as a second, independent drafter |
| **MineCEraft** (UIUC, arXiv 2608.28884, Aug 28 2026) [V] https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.28884 | 723 expert construction instructions, Mindcraft agent, **rule-based programmatic checks** (BFS ground connectivity, span, safety, planning) | Strict problem-level accuracy: gpt5-mini 39.6%, gemini-3-pro 38.3%, claude-4.5-sonnet 26.6%, llama-4 0.4%; humans ~90% | Reliability/physics is the weak spot → **deterministic validators are mandatory**; their check types (connectivity, support, spans) are exactly what we need |
| **MineAnyBuild** (NeurIPS 2025 D&B) [V] https://arxiv.org/html/2505.20148v3 | 4,000 tasks; models output executable 3D block matrices; Mineflayer builds | GPT-4o best 41.02/100; small models can't produce executable plans; large ones misuse block combinations | Raw coordinates/matrices are a bad interface; also notes human raters fatigue after ~10 builds → keep review batches small |
| **APT** (UCLA, arXiv 2411.17255) [V] https://huggingface.co/papers/2411.17255 | CoT decomposition → blueprint; memory + reflection modules | A/B: memory module significantly improves; emergent scaffolding | Keep a growing library of solved sub-problems |
| **T2BM** (IEEE CoG 2024, arXiv 2406.08751) [V] https://arxiv.org/html/2406.08751 | Prompt refinement → interlayer representation → **repair** | Complete buildings with doors/windows/beds when prompted well | Intermediate representation + repair step |
| **Word2Minecraft** (NYU, arXiv 2503.16536) [V] https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.16536 | Story → tile map → scaled structures; ablation | LLM block selection mattered more than the scaling algorithm | Narrative → layout is feasible; materials choice needs constraints |
| **SceneCraft** (ICML 2024) [V] https://arxiv.org/html/2403.01248 | Scene graph → Python constraints → solver → Blender render → GPT-V critique (inner loop) + **library learning** (outer loop) | +45.1%/40.9% CLIP vs BlenderGPT; constraint pass 88.9 vs 5.6 | **Graph-first + render critique + reusable function library** |
| **LL3M** (UChicago, arXiv 2508.08228) [V] https://arxiv.org/html/2508.08228 | Planner, retrieval (BlenderRAG docs), coder, **critic on renders**, verifier, user feedback | Expressive assets; RAG of API docs improves code correctness | Ground the coder in version-pinned docs; critic + verifier + human |
| Code-as-Room (2026) [V] https://arxiv.org/html/2605.18451 | Image → agentic Blender code for rooms | — | Same code-as-asset pattern |
| CraftUtopia (AAMAS 2026 best demo) [V] https://cyprusconferences.org/aamas2026/best-demonstration-award/ | Multi-agent collaborative construction | addresses "low success rates, reliance on predefined templates" | Multi-agent embodied building is still a research demo |
| Voyager (2023) [V] https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291 | Code-as-action + skill library + self-verification | Lifelong skill reuse | Same library idea |
| Community 2026 [C] | YouTube "Opus 5.5 vs GPT 6 Astra mega structures" (Opus 52 min vs Astra 93 min for 7 builds; ~7.5/10 subjective) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JgG4PGN4Ok4 ; r/Minecraft backlash against fake "AI build" images https://www.reddit.com/r/Minecraft/comments/1u25xj5/ | Big impressive massings; interiors/details and buildability are where they fail | Use AI for massing + modules, enforce buildability with checks, let the user judge taste |

**Synthesis [?]:** quality comes from (1) a small typed vocabulary (modules + palette slots + primitives), (2) a plan the user can read (layout graph, blockout), (3) deterministic checks, (4) renders the model and the user both look at, (5) a library that grows with every approved piece. One-shot raw generation is not the path for a hero map.

## 4. Review loop without a GPU

### 4.1 Renderers
| Tool | Runs where | Inputs | Mod blocks | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **deepslate 0.27.2 + headless-gl (`gl`)** | **Cloud, CPU (Mesa llvmpipe) under Xvfb** | Structure from NBT; resources from vanilla assets (misode/mcmeta `1.21.1-summary` + `1.21.1-atlas`) + our resource pack | Yes if we feed our blockstates/models/textures [?] | **Tested today**: npm installed prebuilt `gl` for Node 22; atlas must be padded to power-of-two; needs a fake `gl.canvas` `{clientWidth, clientHeight}`; 8,082-block 64×24×64 structure → 1024×768 PNG in **5.9 s** incl. asset load [V-local]. ### 4.2 Render sheet spec for builds [?]
- Per tile/module: 4 isometric yaw angles (45/135/225/315), top-down plan, **cutaway per floor/Y-band** (roofs hide interiors), critical-path overlay (coloured path voxels from the walkability solver), palette swatch strip, block counts.
- Fixed camera presets so sheets are comparable across revisions (VLM-judging guidance in pipeline doc: fixed 6–24 renders, two model families, order-swapped).
- Diffs: per-tile voxel diff (added/removed/changed counts + highlighted render), and the structure-viewer Compare link for the user.

### 4.3 Deterministic checks to run before any render [?, check types grounded in MineCEraft]
1. **Block-state validity**: every `Name[Properties]` exists in 1.21.1 `--reports/blocks.json` (vanilla) or our mod's block dump (DataDump mod is AGPL and 1.21.1 Fabric-only ✓ [V] https://github.com/tyzeron/MinecraftDataDump → simpler: a 20-line dump command in our own mod).
2. **Item/BE NBT format**: 1.20.5+ components only.
3. **Walkability/reachability**: voxel graph for a 0.6×1.8 player (2 air above a solid/stair/slab top), step 1 (slab/stair rules), jump 1, safe drop ≤3, ladders/vines/scaffolding; BFS along the layout graph's required edges (checkpoint → boss door → shortcut back). Shortcut doors must be one-way where the graph says so.
4. **Support/stability**: no unsupported gravity blocks (sand, gravel, concrete powder), no floating debris unless tagged intentional.
5. **Budgets** (propose to `.ai/contracts/perf-budget.yaml`, human approval): block entities per chunk, light sources per chunk (colored-light shaders), item_display/Animated Java entities per area, total placed blocks per tile.
6. **Palette conformance**: blocks only from the area's palette slots + allowed accents (art-bible).
7. **Diff guard**: changes outside the ticket's tiles fail the gate (one writer per ticket).

## 5. Recommended AI building pipeline for our map

### 5.1 Artifacts and folders [?]
```
.ai/contracts/levels/<area>.layout.yaml   # human-approved layout graph (nodes, edges, gates, shortcuts, sightlines, boss arenas)
.ai/contracts/palettes/<area>.yaml        # palette slots + weathering ramps, derived from art-bible.yaml
world/kits/<kit>/<module>.snbt            # agent-made modules (text, diffable) + <module>.meta.yaml (sockets, tags, footprint)
world/gen/                                # Python assembler (seeded) + validators
world/build/<area>/tiles/*.nbt            # generated output (DataVersion 3955), not hand-edited
world/build/<area>/manifest.json          # tile → position, rotation, checksum
data/<ns>/structure/<area>/...            # shipped copies for /place and GameTests
.ai/evidence/<ticket>/                    # validator logs, render sheets, diff sheets
```
- Module grid: footprints in multiples of 8 (sewer corridors) / 16 (district blocks); heights in 4/8; sockets typed (`sewer_3w`, `door_2x3`, `catwalk_1w`, `drop_3`, `ladder`) [?].
- Palette slots are written as placeholder blocks in modules (e.g. a reserved set of concrete colours) and swapped at assembly → one module serves several areas and decay levels [?].

### 5.2 Stages and gates
| # | Stage | Who makes / tool | Gate (evidence) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Reference + layout graph**: area map, critical path, cycles/shortcuts back to each checkpoint (묘목), arena sizes, vistas | Opus drafts YAML + a schematic 2D diagram; user approves | G0 schema; user approval (G8-lite) |
| 2 | **Palette contract** per area from art-bible (sewer: deepslate tiles, stone bricks, iron bars, chains, copper/oxidized pipes, 흑니 black-mud custom blocks; slums: scrap, planks, terracotta, corrugated look via trapdoors) | Opus/Sonnet; user approves swatch render | palette render sheet |
| 3 | **Module kit** (20–60 modules/area) | One writer per kit (Sonnet/Opus). Optionally a second independent draft by GPT-6.1 Sol (MineBench: near-Opus spatial code at ~1/10 cost) in a separate file; user picks | validators 1–6 per module; render sheet per module; **user approves kit once** |
| 4 | **Greybox assembly** of the layout with plain blocks | Seeded Python assembler (nbtlib + numpy); graph → grid embedding, socket matching (WFC/backtracking for filler) | walkability BFS on required edges; user **playtests the greybox** in game (cheap to change) |
| 5 | **Dressing passes**: palette swap, weathering (noise masks, `integrity`-style decay, Grimoire-style "nooks"), lighting, set-dressing props (Blockbench props from the model pipeline) | assembler passes | validators 1–7; diff sheet vs greybox |
| 6 | **Render review** | deepslate headless sheets in cloud (§4.2) → Claude self-check + VLM triage → user via structure-viewer link (compare mode) | user feedback in ticket `note` |
| 7 | **Integration** | 1.21.1 NeoForge dedicated server (CI or PC) + RCON: `/forceload`, `/place template` per tile; or WorldEdit `//schem load` + `//perf neighbors off` on the PC | GameTests for encounter rooms (spawners, doors, triggers), boot-log scan |
| 8 | **Terrain base** (outer ruins, lake shore) | WorldPainter `wpscript` from a heightmap PNG (agent-drawn), then tiles placed on top; terrain read back with amulet-core for foundations/stilts | heightmap/route overlay render |
| 9 | **Mood check** | user PC: Iris + chosen shader screenshots along a fixed camera path (langyo MCP) | G5/G6 frame time + user approval (G8) |

### 5.3 Rules that keep quality high [?]
- Never let the model emit large raw coordinate lists; it writes **code** against our helpers (`box`, `line`, `stairs_run`, `arch`, `pipe`, `place_module(socket)`) — the MineBench/MC-Bench pattern.
- The **world save is a build output**; the source of truth is contracts + modules + generator + seeds. Rebuild deterministically; commit SNBT/meta, not region files.
- Tile the world (e.g. 32×32 or 48×48 column tiles, full height of the area) so reviews, diffs and `/place` calls stay small; 48 also keeps tiles loadable by a structure block [?].
- Version pinning: assets for renders from mcmeta `1.21.1-*` branches; block validation from 1.21.1 reports; no 1.21.2+ blocks/commands (`/place ... strict`, pale oak etc.).
- Taste stays with the user: keep review batches ≤10 items (rater fatigue, MineAnyBuild F.7), always show the previous approved version beside the new one.
